ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-image information gain of views in small-batch SimCLR
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR with a ResNet-18 backbone on CIFAR-10 at batch size 256. Estimate how much information the second view adds beyond the first for an image, using a variational InfoNCE bound against a bank of 4096 stored embeddings. Track this gain over 200 epochs, then reweight the contrastive loss by it so that low-gain pairs count less. Report linear probe and 20-nearest-neighbour accuracy over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Plain SimCLR with the same schedule; reweighting by randomly shuffled gains; reweighting by the per-image loss value alone, to test whether the gain carries more than difficulty; a batch size 1024 reference run.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Gain reweighting should raise linear probe accuracy by roughly 1 to 2 points at batch 256 and close part of the gap to batch 1024. It could fail if the bound is too noisy at small batch to rank images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Information gain of augmented views tracked with a ResNet-50 backbone on CIFAR-10
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR with a ResNet-50 backbone on CIFAR-10 at batch size 256 for 800 epochs. Measure what the second view contributes beyond the first, using a variational InfoNCE bound against a bank of 4096 stored embeddings, and snapshot the estimate at epochs 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160. Retrain the complete schedule from 5 seeds, apply the gain as a loss weight in a second pass, and evaluate linear probe and 20-nearest-neighbour accuracy at the snapshots.
CONTROLS: Plain SimCLR with the same schedule and backbone; weights drawn from shuffled gains; weights from the per-image loss value alone; a reference run at batch size 1024.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Weighting by gain should move linear probe accuracy up by about 1 to 2 points and narrow the batch-size gap on this dataset. It could fail if gain estimates fluctuate between seeds too much to give a stable ranking.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned view generator with a semantic-consistency constraint
PROPOSAL: Train a small convolutional generator that proposes residual perturbations to an image, added to the usual crop and colour jitter, inside a SimCLR loop with a ResNet-18 backbone at batch size 128. Constrain the generator by keeping the frozen-teacher embedding of the perturbed view within a cosine radius of the original, and reward it for lowering the agreement between views. Run on CIFAR-100 and STL-10, evaluating linear probe accuracy over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: SimCLR with hand-tuned augmentation only; a generator without the consistency constraint; random noise perturbations of matched norm; SimCLR at batch size 512 as a larger-batch reference.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The constrained generator should add around 1.5 points of linear probe accuracy at batch 128 over hand-tuned views. It could fail if the generator drifts toward perturbations that destroy class content and the constraint is too loose to stop it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned view generator across five datasets with repeated retraining
PROPOSAL: Train a convolutional generator that proposes residual perturbations to an image on top of the standard crop and colour jitter, inside a SimCLR loop with a ResNet-18 backbone at batch size 128. Keep the frozen-teacher embedding of the perturbed view within a cosine radius of the original, and train the generator to lower agreement between views. Run the full pipeline on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, Tiny-ImageNet and Flowers-102, retraining from scratch with 5 seeds, and report linear probe accuracy.
CONTROLS: SimCLR with hand-tuned augmentation only; a generator without the consistency constraint; random noise perturbations of matched norm; SimCLR at batch size 512.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Across these datasets the constrained generator should give a gain of 1 to 2 points in linear probe accuracy at batch 128. It could fail on the datasets with fine-grained classes, where perturbations may erase the cues that separate neighbours.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent-space positive expansion for MoCo with a small queue
PROPOSAL: Add synthetic positives to MoCo v2 by interpolating between the query embedding and its key embedding, with the mixing coefficient drawn from a Beta distribution, and treat the interpolants as extra keys in the InfoNCE denominator numerator. Use a ResNet-18 backbone, CIFAR-100, a queue of 1024 entries and 200 epochs. Report linear probe accuracy and alignment and uniformity statistics over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: MoCo v2 with the same queue and no interpolation; interpolation with the mixing coefficient fixed at 0.5; a queue of 4096 entries without interpolation as a memory-heavy reference.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Interpolated positives should improve linear probe accuracy by roughly 1 point with a 1024-entry queue and improve uniformity. It could fail if interpolants collapse toward the query and stop adding useful diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Queue size and backbone study of MoCo v2 on one dataset
PROPOSAL: Train MoCo v2 with a ResNet-50 backbone on CIFAR-100 using a queue of 1024 entries for 400 epochs, adding synthetic positives built by interpolating between the query and key embeddings with a coefficient drawn from a Beta distribution. Retrain the whole run at queue sizes 256, 1024, 4096, 8192 and 16384 with 5 seeds, and report linear probe accuracy together with alignment and uniformity statistics.
CONTROLS: MoCo v2 with identical queue size and no interpolation; interpolation with the coefficient fixed at 0.5; a queue of 4096 entries without interpolation.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Interpolated positives should improve linear probe accuracy by roughly 1 point at the smallest queue and improve uniformity. It could fail if the benefit vanishes at queue sizes where negatives already supply diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mapping invariance against expressivity under varying augmentation strength
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR with a ResNet-18 backbone on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 at 5 levels of crop and colour augmentation strength. At epochs 50, 100 and 200, measure view alignment, uniformity, the effective rank of the embedding covariance and a linear probe on the frozen features. Fit how the probe accuracy responds to alignment and effective rank jointly, using 3 seeds, and locate the strength where the trade-off peaks per dataset.
CONTROLS: A supervised ResNet-18 trained on the same data as an upper reference; a randomly initialised encoder as a lower reference; SimCLR runs with the strength fixed at the common default; a regression using alignment only as predictor.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Probe accuracy should peak at intermediate strength and effective rank should fall as strength grows. It could fail if the optimum shifts between the datasets so much that no shared curve describes the trade-off.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Invariance and expressivity measured on ImageNet-100 with a ResNet-50 backbone
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR with a ResNet-50 backbone on ImageNet-100 at 5 levels of crop and colour augmentation strength for 300 epochs. At epochs 25, 50, 100, 200 and 300, record view alignment, uniformity, the effective rank of the embedding covariance and a linear probe on the frozen features. Repeat the whole sweep from 5 seeds and fit probe accuracy jointly against alignment and effective rank to locate the strength at which the trade-off peaks.
CONTROLS: A supervised ResNet-50 trained on the same data as an upper reference; a randomly initialised encoder as a lower reference; SimCLR runs at the common default strength; a regression with alignment alone as predictor.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Probe accuracy should peak at intermediate strength while effective rank falls as strength increases. It could fail if seed-to-seed spread is as large as the differences between neighbouring strengths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-cached small-batch contrastive training against large-batch SimCLR
PROPOSAL: Compare SimCLR at batch size 64 with a gradient-caching variant that simulates a batch of 1024 by accumulating embeddings before the backward pass, using a ResNet-18 backbone on CIFAR-100 for 300 epochs. Add an instance-wise view expansion that draws 4 views instead of 2 per image at batch 64. Report linear probe accuracy and wall-clock memory use over 3 seeds, so the trade between batch size and view count is visible.
CONTROLS: SimCLR at batch 64 with 2 views; SimCLR at batch 1024 with 2 views; gradient caching without view expansion; 4 views at batch 64 with the views drawn from the same augmentation pipeline as the baseline.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Four views at batch 64 should recover most of the accuracy gap to batch 1024 at far lower memory. It could fail if extra views from the same pipeline are too correlated to add information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: View count against batch size on one dataset with repeated runs
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR with a ResNet-34 backbone on CIFAR-100 for 300 epochs, varying the number of views per image over 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 at batch sizes 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024. Retrain each configuration from 3 seeds and report linear probe accuracy and memory use, then fit accuracy as a function of batch size and view count to see where one substitutes for the other.
CONTROLS: The 2-view configuration at every batch size; gradient caching at batch 64 without extra views; views drawn with the same augmentation pipeline in all settings.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Added views should recover most of the accuracy lost at batch 64, with returns that flatten past 4 views. It could fail if views from one pipeline are too correlated for the curve to bend at all.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing augmentations by estimated information gain on STL-10
PROPOSAL: Score candidate augmentation policies by the mutual information between views estimated with a variational InfoNCE critic, then select the policy with the highest score under a semantic-consistency filter based on a frozen teacher. Train SimCLR with a ResNet-50 backbone on STL-10 at batch size 128 for 400 epochs with 5 candidate policies, including RandAugment and the SimCLR default, and report linear probe accuracy over 3 seeds together with the rank correlation between score and accuracy.
CONTROLS: SimCLR default and RandAugment as fixed policies; a randomly picked policy; selection by the loss at epoch 20 instead of the information score; selection with the filter removed.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The information score should rank policies with a Spearman correlation above 0.6 against probe accuracy. It could fail if the critic rewards views that differ in nuisance factors and thereby prefers policies that harm semantics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy scoring by mutual information on a ResNet-18 backbone across 5 policies
PROPOSAL: Estimate the mutual information between views with a variational InfoNCE critic for 5 candidate augmentation policies and keep the highest scorer that passes a frozen-teacher consistency filter. Train SimCLR with a ResNet-18 backbone at batch size 128 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and STL-10 for 200 epochs, including RandAugment and the SimCLR default among the candidates, and report linear probe accuracy over 5 seeds with the rank correlation between score and accuracy.
CONTROLS: SimCLR default and RandAugment as fixed policies; a randomly picked policy; selection by the loss at epoch 20; selection with the filter removed; selection by the critic trained for 2 epochs only.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The information score should rank policies with a Spearman correlation above 0.6 against probe accuracy on the three datasets. It could fail if the critic favours views that differ in nuisance factors and so prefers harmful policies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spectral view of per-instance gain in a trained contrastive encoder
PROPOSAL: Take a SimCLR ResNet-18 checkpoint trained on CIFAR-10 and build a k-nearest-neighbour graph on the embeddings with k set to 15. Compute for every image the drop in nearest-neighbour agreement when its second view is replaced by a random augmentation, and relate this gain to the degree and the second eigenvector of the graph Laplacian. Report rank correlations with bootstrap intervals from 3 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: A shuffled-image null for the correlation; a graph built from raw pixels instead of embeddings; the gain computed with a different random augmentation set; a supervised ResNet-18 encoder as a contrast.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Gain should correlate with Laplacian degree at a Spearman value near 0.4. It could fail if the correlation is driven by class imbalance in neighbourhoods rather than by view information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-image view gain related to graph structure across checkpoints and datasets
PROPOSAL: Take SimCLR ResNet-50 checkpoints trained on CIFAR-10 and build a nearest-neighbour graph on the embeddings with k set to 15. Compute the drop in neighbour agreement when the second view is replaced by a random augmentation, and relate this gain to the degree and the second eigenvector of the graph Laplacian. Save the checkpoints at 8 time points and retrain from 5 seeds, then report rank correlations with bootstrap intervals at each time point.
CONTROLS: A shuffled-image null for the correlation; a graph built from raw pixels; the gain computed with a different random augmentation set; a supervised ResNet-50 encoder.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Gain should correlate with Laplacian degree at a Spearman value near 0.4 once training has progressed. It could fail if class imbalance in neighbourhoods drives the effect instead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gain-driven number of views per image
PROPOSAL: Let the number of views drawn for an image depend on its running information gain: images whose second view added little receive 4 more views in the next epoch, while saturated images stay at 2. Train MoCo v2 with a ResNet-50 backbone on ImageNet-100 at batch size 128 for 100 epochs and report linear probe accuracy over 2 seeds along with the average number of views used.
CONTROLS: A fixed 2-view MoCo v2; a fixed 4-view MoCo v2; a random assignment of views matched to the same average count; a gain schedule using the loss value as a stand-in.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Adaptive allocation should match the 4-view run within 0.5 points while using close to 2.7 views on average. It could fail if the gain signal is too noisy early in training and the allocation tracks batch composition instead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fixed view counts compared on CIFAR-100 with repeated retraining
PROPOSAL: Train MoCo v2 with a ResNet-18 backbone on CIFAR-100 using fixed view counts of 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 for 400 epochs at batch size 128. Retrain the whole sweep from 5 seeds and report linear probe accuracy and the training time per epoch, then compare against a version that assigns more views to images whose second view added little in the previous epoch, estimated with the same bound.
CONTROLS: A fixed 2-view MoCo v2; a fixed 4-view MoCo v2; a random assignment of views matched to the same average count; a schedule using the loss value in place of the gain.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Adaptive allocation should match the 4-view run within 0.5 points at lower average view count. It could fail if the signal is too noisy early in training and merely tracks batch composition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semantic-consistency regulariser from a frozen teacher
PROPOSAL: Add a consistency term to SimCLR that penalises divergence between the student's view embedding and a momentum teacher's embedding of the clean image, weighted by a coefficient in 0.1, 0.5 and 1.0. Use a ResNet-18 backbone, CIFAR-100, batch size 256 and 300 epochs with strong crop augmentation, and report linear probe accuracy and kNN accuracy over 3 seeds, plus accuracy as a function of crop scale lower bound.
CONTROLS: SimCLR with strong augmentation and no term; SimCLR with weak augmentation; the term with a stop-gradient removed; a term using a randomly initialised teacher.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The regulariser should recover about 2 points lost to strong augmentation at crop scale 0.08. It could fail if the teacher's clean embedding carries so little class structure that the term only damps learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-guided consistency with a larger student on one dataset
PROPOSAL: Add a consistency term to SimCLR that penalises divergence between the student's view embedding and a momentum teacher's embedding of the clean image, using a ResNet-50 student and teacher on CIFAR-100 at batch size 256 for 600 epochs. Test coefficients 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0, retrain from 5 seeds, and report linear probe accuracy and kNN accuracy, plus accuracy against the crop scale lower bound.
CONTROLS: SimCLR with strong augmentation and no term; SimCLR with weak augmentation; the term without stop-gradient; a term using a randomly initialised teacher.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The term should recover about 2 points lost to strong augmentation at crop scale 0.08. It could fail if the clean embedding has too little class structure and the term mainly slows learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Information-gain curriculum for augmentation strength on ImageNet-100
PROPOSAL: Raise augmentation strength during SimCLR training only while the per-image information gain of views stays above a threshold, estimated by a variational InfoNCE critic updated online. Train a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 at batch size 256 for 400 epochs, with 2 seeds, and compare linear probe accuracy and number of epochs to a target accuracy. Include a ResNet-18 run on CIFAR-100 to check that the schedule transfers.
CONTROLS: Fixed default strength; a linear ramp of strength with the same endpoints; a ramp set by training loss instead of gain; the critic frozen after 20 epochs.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The curriculum should reach the target probe accuracy in roughly 30 % fewer epochs. It could fail if the critic estimate lags the encoder so that strength rises too slowly or too fast.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmentation strength schedules compared on CIFAR-100 with a ResNet-50 backbone
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR with a ResNet-50 backbone on CIFAR-100 at batch size 256 for 800 epochs under 6 schedules of augmentation strength, among them a gain-driven one that raises strength while a variational InfoNCE critic reports high information gain. Retrain from 5 seeds, record the number of epochs to reach a target probe accuracy, and report final linear probe accuracy with a ResNet-18 repeat on the same dataset.
CONTROLS: Fixed default strength; a linear ramp with the same endpoints; a ramp set by training loss; the critic frozen after 20 epochs; a cosine ramp.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The gain-driven schedule should reach the target in roughly 30 % fewer epochs. It could fail if the critic lags the encoder so that strength rises at the wrong pace.
